parsed.attack: The audience is defined by an intersection - parent of an under-five AND closest friends three or more time zones away - which shrinks an already low-ARPU notification category to a segment no channel can target, and the named shareable_artifact loop does not exist, because a computed time-zone overlap window is not something anyone posts. That leaves paid acquisition, where a digest utility prices at $2.99-4.99 ($2.54-4.24 net) and their own 3% conversion floor puts a payer at $195 on iOS and $64 on Android: 57 and 19 months of payback. Marginal cost is genuinely near zero, so the margin half of this attack fails - but a product with zero COGS, no viral artifact, a sub-median price and a 57-month iOS payback has no route to scale at all.
parsed.strongest_defence: COGS is zero and the developer is one person, so the only requirement is organic installs; parenting and expat communities are dense and free, the brief is a daily habit rather than an occasional utility which supports $4.99, and unlike a reminder app the value compounds with calendar history so churn should be lower than the category.
parsed.verdict_reason: Free to run, but the only named distribution loop is not a real artifact and paid acquisition needs 19-57 months of payback, so there is no channel that scales.
